source.citation: Zenodo record 20394352, 'Optimising Spectral Composition in Hydroponic Lettuce Cultivation: The Role of Green Light, Open Data'. Author list per the Zenodo landing page.

design.confoundedTreatment: t3 (spectrum and planting density both change)
design.designNote: Four regimes, not a gradient. The dataset supports comparing named spectral regimes. It does not support fitting a continuous response surface in green-light fraction, because only two regimes hold a fixed spectrum and one of them is the control.

transformations: long-format source kept long; no trait was pivoted into another's place
treatment labels mapped to lower-case regime ids; the source label is kept in the design table as sourceLabel
no unit conversion, no imputation, no outlier removal
limits: One experiment, one cultivar (Red Batavia), one light level (200 umol/m2/s), one photoperiod (16 h).
PPFD and photoperiod are constant across regimes, so this dataset cannot identify a light-intensity or daily-light-integral response.
Ambient CO2 is not reported and not varied; nothing here supports a CO2 response.
Green-light fraction is given by the source as a percentage of the spectrum, not as a measured spectral power distribution; the control value is the source's own approximation.
